The server-side auth probe doesn't "see" a browser session directly — it never has access to the browser's own cookie jar during SSR. This interceptor is the mechanism that gives the server-side probe a "session" at all: since Angular Universal's server-side `HttpClient` runs in Node with no browser cookie storage, this interceptor forwards the cookies from the original incoming request (the one the browser sent to the Node/SSR server) onto the outgoing API call, so the backend sees the same session cookie it would have seen from the browser directly.

Invoice creation in this codebase is decoupled from payment success via the domain-event pattern: subsystem [11] (Subscriptions, payments & consent) emits `InvoiceCreatedEvent.java` (Event, [11]), which affects `InvoiceRecord.java` (the invoice entity/status record) and is picked up by `InvoiceCreatedEventListener.java`. That's the `@TransactionalEventListener` decoupling pattern the graph flags for subsystem [12], applied here for billing: the listener only fires after the triggering transaction commits, so invoice-record creation/sync to the accounting system (Fakturownia, via `InvoicingPort.java` / `FakturowniaInvoiceResponse.java`) is not synchronous with the Stripe payment webhook.
